summary: Concurrent logins from new geolocations after forwarded vendor email
description: Issue summary: An employee reported a suspicious vendor email they had forwarded to a colleague; within ~30 minutes multiple concurrent sessions for the same employee account were observed from two geographically distinct IPs. Impact: Possible account takeover or session replay; user tokens may have been exposed. Affected user: j.singh@redwood.com. Timeline (UTC): 2026-03-12T17:48:00Z - Employee received and forwarded vendor email; 2026-03-12T18:22:00Z - New session from 198.51.100.42 (approx EU region) authenticated without MFA prompt; 2026-03-12T18:24:30Z - Concurrent session from 203.0.113.88 (APAC-range) established; 2026-03-12T18:28:00Z - Employee reported email to SOC and forwarded original message. Environment: prod, SSO (Okta), Redwood Console, API gateway and serving runtime all in us-east primary region. Steps to reproduce / actions taken: 1) Reviewed Okta authentication logs for j.singh@redwood.com and confirmed two successful session creations within 3 minutes from different IP ranges. 2) Checked device fingerprint and user agent: session A shows corporate-managed MacOS + Redwood VPN tag; session B shows generic Chrome on Windows and no corporate VPN. 3) Verified MFA enrollment: user has MFA enabled and primary factor is TOTP + WebAuthn. 4) Rotated user's API keys and forced logout of all sessions via admin console. Observed evidence: authentication logs, session IDs (sid-A, sid-B), access patterns showing list/list endpoint calls from sid-B that the user denies. Initial hypothesis: forwarded email contained either a malicious link that triggered client-side credential capture or the user inadvertently forwarded a session cookie/token attachment (less likely). Another possibility is a compromised vendor system that relayed session tokens. Immediate mitigations applied: - Forced global logout and session invalidation for j.singh@redwood.com at 2026-03-12T18:40:00Z. - Blocked IPs 198.51.100.42 and 203.0.113.88 at firewall and added to temporary denylist. - Reset user's Okta refresh tokens and required re-auth with MFA. - Instructed user to change passwords on external services and to preserve the original forwarded email as evidence. Next steps requested: - Deep packet/log analysis for the two IPs and any parent ASN to track origin. - Endpoint scan of reporting employee's device by IT/Endpoint team. - Triage the forwarded email contents (headers, links, attachments) to determine if token leakage occurred. - Check session cookie entropy and issuance endpoints for anomalies. - If evidence of compromise, escalate to InfoSec incident response and consider org-wide suspect email alert. Links: Slack #sec-ops thread https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234567, Okta auth log link https://okta.redwood.com/logs?user=j.singh, runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/sec/incident-response
comments: SOC - 2026-03-12T18:35Z: User reported forwarded vendor email; observed concurrent sessions in Okta. Forced logout and token rotation executed. Blocking suspicious IPs. Assigning to Marco for deeper auth analysis.

Marco Li - 2026-03-12T19:10Z: Reviewed Okta session records. sid-B (203.0.113.88) shows no VPN tag and a UA string matching headless Chrome. No obvious successful privilege elevation seen yet. Pulling gateway logs and API access patterns now.
IT Endpoint - 2026-03-12T20:05Z: Requested endpoint scan; user machine shows last patch on 2026-02-28. Running EDR scan now; will share results in channel.

Aisha Park - 2026-03-12T20:30Z: User confirms they only forwarded the email body and link to a colleague, did not attach files. Colleague reports not clicking link. Preserving email headers and original message.

InfoSec - 2026-03-13T09:00Z: Escalating to IR team if we find evidence of token exfiltration or lateral activity. Please collect full packet captures if possible; otherwise, save gateway logs for 24h rolling window.
investigation_notes: Logs reviewed: Okta auth events, gateway access logs (api-gateway), console audit trail, and user workstation EDR scan. Key artefacts: two session ids (sid-A, sid-B); sid-B client UA: 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 HeadlessChrome/105.0'; both sessions used the same account but different refresh token IDs. No immediate evidence of token reuse across other accounts. Checked audit trail for privilege changes: none. Searched for similar IPs or UAs across tenant: found 3 other auth attempts from 203.0.113.88 to service accounts historically (older than 30 days). Related runbooks and links: https://confluence.redwood.com/sec/ir-playbooks/suspicious-session, Slack #sec-ops. Hypothesis: credential or session token interception due to malicious link opened in non-corporate browser or a vendor-side leak. Next investigative actions: ASN lookup for 198.51.100.42 and 203.0.113.88, request full packet logs from edge for the time window, cross-check with identity provider for any abnormal token issuance flows, and request vendor to provide activity logs for the forwarded message.
resolution_notes: Triage ongoing. No confirmed domain-wide compromise as of latest update. Temporary mitigations applied (global logout, token rotation, IP blocks). Awaiting endpoint scan results and packet logs. If evidence of compromise found, IR team to initiate full incident response and customer communication as required.
